speaker_role: student/recent applicant (self-described college freshman, successful T20/Ivy-track applicant), not an admissions officer or counselor
commercial_incentive: none evident beyond promoting his own channel/content; explicitly dismisses school counselors and generic online advice as unreliable
key_insights: Recommends picking a tentative career/major direction as early as freshman year (via shadowing, clubs, competitions) rather than waiting, arguing early exploration allows later pivots without losing application 'positioning'
Suggests limiting freshman year to 2-3 clubs pursued deeply (regular attendance, competition, leadership pipeline) rather than sampling many clubs broadly
Recommends a shadowing experience (roughly 60-80 hours for medicine, 20-30 hours for other fields) and ideally a paid or unpaid internship between freshman and sophomore summer

Advises choosing SAT or ACT in fall of sophomore year, prepping through the year, and testing in August before junior year to avoid conflicting with junior-year workload; suggests targeting roughly 1500 SAT / 34+ ACT

Suggests reserving junior year mostly for coursework/GPA and existing activities, starting essays in second semester junior year, and aiming to submit most applications by the end of the following summer
Frames one cohesive, self-driven project (his example: a nonprofit) built up over sophomore year as a stronger differentiator than many disconnected activities
specific_numbers_or_facts: Suggested shadowing hours: roughly 60-80 hours total for medicine-track shadowing, 20-30 hours for other fields (presenter's own recommendation, not sourced data)
Suggested test-prep target: SAT ~1500+ / ACT 34+ (presenter's own recommendation)
Presenter states he personally submitted 'nine or ten' college applications by the end of summer before senior year (self-reported)
notable_or_distinctive: Presents an explicit month-by-month, year-by-year personal planning roadmap (including his own Google Sheets planning tool) rather than generic tips, aimed at students targeting Ivy/T20 admission.
reliability_notes: Entirely one student's individual opinion/anecdote framed as universal strategy, with dismissive framing toward school counselors and other online advice; numeric benchmarks are his own opinions, not institutional data; informal, hyperbolic language throughout.
